stimuli.title: EVS passage: The Chipko Movement
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the early 1970s, many trees in the hills of the Garhwal Himalaya, in today's Uttarakhand, were being cut down for timber. The village people needed these forests. Women collected firewood, fodder for their animals and fruits from them. The roots of the trees also held the soil on the steep slopes, so cutting the trees meant more landslides and floods.

In 1974, when workers came to cut trees near the village of Reni, a group of women led by Gaura Devi stood in their way. They put their arms around the trees and refused to move. The word 'chipko' means 'to hug' or 'to stick to'. The workers had to go back.

The Chipko Movement spread to many villages and taught people across India that forests must be protected.

stimuli.title: Passage 1
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

Meena lived in a small village near the river. Her school had only a few books, and she had read all of them twice. One evening she said to her grandfather, 'If every family gives one old book, we can have a library.'

Grandfather smiled and helped her write a notice. They pinned it to the big neem tree near the well. At first only two books came. Meena did not give up. She went from house to house with her friend Salim, and soon the shelf in Grandfather's room was full of storybooks, old magazines and even a dictionary.

Every Sunday, children gathered under the neem tree to read. Some older people who had never learnt to read came to listen. Meena felt proud, but she said the library belonged to the whole village.

stimuli.title: Passage 2
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

The Indian elephant is the largest land animal in Asia. A grown elephant can weigh as much as several cars. Its trunk is its nose and upper lip joined together, and it is so useful that the elephant can pick up a single peanut or pull down a branch with it. Elephants also use their trunks to drink, to smell and to greet one another.

Elephants live in herds led by the oldest female, who remembers the paths to water and food. They eat grass, leaves, bark and fruit, and spend most of the day eating. Because they need large forests, elephants are in danger when forests are cut down. In India, the elephant is honoured as the national heritage animal.

stimuli.title: Passage 3
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

On the morning of Makar Sankranti, the sky over Ahmedabad was full of kites. Arjun climbed to the roof with his cousin Neha. Their kite was red and yellow, with a long paper tail.

Neha held the spool of string while Arjun ran across the roof and let the kite go. A gust of wind lifted it high above the water tanks. 'Let out more string!' Arjun shouted. Soon their kite was dancing with hundreds of others.

Suddenly another kite crossed theirs, and the string snapped. The red and yellow kite drifted away over the rooftops. Arjun's face fell. Then Neha laughed and pointed at the sky. 'Look, it is flying free now,' she said. Arjun began to smile too, and they ran downstairs to make a new one.

stimuli.title: Passage 4
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the hills of West Bengal runs one of the most famous little railways in the world, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway. People call it the toy train because its engines and coaches are small and the track is narrow, only about two feet wide.

The line climbs from the plains near Siliguri up to Darjeeling, high in the mountains. To climb the steep hills, the track goes round in loops and even zigzags back and forth. At some places the train runs so close to houses and shops that people can almost touch it.

The railway was opened more than a hundred years ago. Today it is a World Heritage Site, and visitors from many countries come to ride it and enjoy the views of the snowy peaks.

stimuli.title: EVS passage: Saving rain in the desert
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the Thar Desert of western Rajasthan, it rains on only a few days in a year, so every drop of water is precious. Many families there build a kund, an underground tank shaped like a round bowl with a dome on top. The ground around the kund is made to slope gently towards it, so that when rain falls, the water runs into the tank. The dome keeps out dust and stops the water from drying up in the hot sun.

People draw water from the kund with a bucket and use it for drinking all through the dry months. Animals such as camels and goats are given water from the village ponds. In this way, desert people have learnt to collect and save rainwater for the whole year.

stimuli.title: Passage 1
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

Raju's grandmother was a potter. Every morning she sat at her wheel in the courtyard, her hands wet with clay. As the wheel spun, a lump of clay rose and turned into a pot, a lamp or a small cup.

Raju loved to watch her. One day he asked if he could try. Grandmother let him sit at the wheel. His first pot leaned to one side and then collapsed. His second pot cracked as it dried in the sun. Raju wanted to stop, but Grandmother said, 'Even my first pots looked like that. Clay teaches patience.'

Before Diwali, Raju finally made twelve small lamps that stood straight and did not crack. He painted them orange and gave them to his neighbours. That evening, his lamps glowed on many doorsteps.

stimuli.title: Passage 2
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A honeybee colony can have thousands of bees, but only one queen. The queen lays the eggs. Most of the other bees are workers, and they do all the jobs in the hive. Young workers clean the cells and feed the baby bees. Older workers fly out to collect nectar and pollen from flowers.

When a worker bee finds a good patch of flowers, she returns to the hive and does a dance. The way she moves tells the other bees in which direction the flowers are and how far away they are.

Bees turn nectar into honey and store it in wax cells. As they move from flower to flower, they also carry pollen, which helps plants make fruits and seeds. Without bees, many of the fruits we eat would be hard to grow.

stimuli.title: Passage 3
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

It had been raining since noon. On her way home from school, Fatima heard a soft whimper under a parked cart. She bent down and saw a small brown puppy, wet and shivering.

Fatima wrapped it in her dupatta and carried it home. Her mother frowned at first, worried about the muddy paws, but then she brought an old towel and a bowl of warm milk. The puppy drank every drop and fell asleep near the stove.

The next day Fatima stuck a notice at the corner shop: 'Found: brown puppy with a white spot on its ear.' In the evening a boy named Kabir came running. The puppy jumped into his arms and licked his face. Kabir thanked Fatima again and again, and promised to bring the puppy to visit her.

stimuli.title: Passage 4
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

For most of India, the monsoon is the most important season of the year. In early summer the land becomes very hot. Winds blowing from the sea towards the land carry a great deal of moisture. When these moist winds reach the land, they bring heavy rain.

The monsoon usually reaches the coast of Kerala in early June and then spreads across the country over the next few weeks. Farmers wait eagerly for it, because many crops, such as rice, depend on the rain. The rain fills rivers, lakes and wells, and gives water for the whole year.

But the monsoon can also cause trouble. Too much rain can flood towns and fields, while a late or weak monsoon can dry up crops. That is why weather scientists study the winds carefully each year.

stimuli.title: EVS passage: How seeds travel
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

Plants cannot walk, yet their seeds travel far from the parent plant. This helps the young plants get enough space, light and water. Some seeds, such as those of the madar plant, have fine hairs and float away on the wind. The coconut has a hard shell with a thick layer of fibre, so it can float on the sea and reach a faraway beach.

Some seeds have tiny hooks that stick to the fur of animals or to our clothes, and drop off somewhere else. The pods of some plants, like balsam, dry up and burst open with a snap, throwing their seeds in all directions. Birds help too, when they eat fruits and drop the seeds far away.

stimuli.title: Passage 1
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

On sports day, Ravi ran in the 400 metre race. He had practised every morning for a month. When the whistle blew, he started fast and was soon in front. Halfway round the track, he heard a cry. His friend Imran had tripped and was sitting on the ground, holding his knee.

Ravi stopped. He went back, helped Imran up and walked with him to the finishing line. Both boys came last. Ravi was sad for a moment, but then the whole school stood up and clapped. At the prize ceremony, the head teacher gave Ravi a special badge for kindness. 'Winning a race is good,' she said, 'but helping a friend is better.'

stimuli.title: Passage 2
stimuli.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A lighthouse is a tall tower built on a rocky coast or on a small island. At the top is a powerful lamp. At night and in fog, the lamp flashes its light far out to sea. Sailors use the light to know where the dangerous rocks are, and to find their way into the harbour.

Each lighthouse flashes in its own pattern. One may flash twice every ten seconds, while another may show a steady light. By counting the flashes, sailors can tell which lighthouse they are looking at.

In the past, a lighthouse keeper lived in the tower and kept the lamp burning all night. Today most lighthouses work automatically, but many are still painted in bright stripes so that they are easy to see in the day.

questions.stem: Which letter comes next in the series? B, D, F, H, ...
questions.explanation: Each letter skips one letter of the alphabet: B (skip C) D (skip E) F (skip G) H, so after skipping I the next is J.

questions.stem: A mirror is held beside each capital letter, to its right. Which letter looks exactly the same in the mirror?
questions.explanation: H has the same left half and right half, so its mirror image is unchanged. N, S and Z all look reversed in a side mirror.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 3, 6, 12, 24, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is double the one before it: 24 x 2 = 48. Adding 12 again would give 36, but the gaps are growing, not staying the same.

questions.stem: A wall clock shows 3:00. What time does the clock seem to show when you look at it in a mirror?
questions.explanation: A mirror swaps left and right, so the hour hand pointing at 3 seems to point at 9. A quick check: the real time and the mirror time add up to 12:00.

questions.stem: Which pair comes next? AM, BN, CO, ...
questions.explanation: Both letters move forward one place each time: A, B, C, D and M, N, O, P. So the next pair is DP.

questions.stem: A square sheet of paper is folded in half once, and one hole is punched through both layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is opened?
questions.explanation: The punch goes through two layers, so it makes two holes, one on each half, placed like mirror images of each other.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 3, 4, 7, 12, 19, ...
questions.explanation: The amount added goes up by 2 each time: +1, +3, +5, +7, then +9. So 19 + 9 = 28.

questions.stem: Both diagonals of a square are drawn. How many triangles of any size can be counted in the figure?
questions.explanation: The diagonals make 4 small triangles. Each diagonal also cuts the square into 2 bigger triangles, which adds 4 more: 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.stem: AB is to CD as PQ is to:
questions.explanation: CD is the pair of letters that comes right after AB. The pair that comes right after PQ is RS.

questions.stem: Which capital letter looks exactly the same in its water image, the reflection in still water below it?
questions.explanation: A water image flips a letter upside down. E has the same top half and bottom half, so it is unchanged. A, M and T look upside down.

questions.stem: Which letter comes next? Y, W, U, S, ...
questions.explanation: The series goes backwards through the alphabet, skipping one letter each time: Y, W, U, S, then Q (R is skipped).

questions.stem: A square piece of paper is cut along one of its diagonals. What two pieces do you get?
questions.explanation: A diagonal joins opposite corners, so each piece has three sides and three corners: two triangles of the same size.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 5, 10, 9, 18, 17, ...
questions.explanation: The rule is double, then take away 1: 5 x 2 = 10, 10 - 1 = 9, 9 x 2 = 18, 18 - 1 = 17, so next is 17 x 2 = 34.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
questions.explanation: A rectangle can be folded exactly in half along its two middle lines, across and down. Folding along a diagonal does not match, so it has 2, not 4 like a square.

questions.stem: Which comes next? A1, C3, E5, G7, ...
questions.explanation: The letters skip one (A, C, E, G, I) and each number is the letter's place in the alphabet: I is the 9th letter, so I9.

questions.stem: Look at the series: triangle, square, pentagon, ... Which shape comes next?
questions.explanation: The shapes have 3, 4 and 5 sides, so the next has 6 sides: a hexagon. A heptagon has 7 sides.

questions.stem: If PEN is written as QFO, how is INK written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter of PEN moves forward one place: P to Q, E to F, N to O. In the same way I becomes J, N becomes O and K becomes L.

questions.stem: An arrow points north. It makes a quarter turn clockwise, then another quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it point now?
questions.explanation: One quarter turn clockwise from north points east; a second quarter turn points south. Two quarter turns make a half turn.

questions.stem: Which number does not fit the series 7, 14, 22, 28, 35?
questions.explanation: The series is the 7 times table: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. The number 22 should be 21.

questions.stem: A big square is divided into a 2 by 2 grid of four small squares. How many squares of any size can be counted?
questions.explanation: There are 4 small squares plus the big square around them, which makes 5.

questions.stem: Which animal is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The tiger is India's national animal. The elephant is the national heritage animal, a different title.

questions.stem: Rice and chapati are rich in which nutrient that gives our body energy?
questions.explanation: Rice and wheat are mostly starch, a carbohydrate, our main source of energy. Proteins, found in pulses and milk, mainly build the body.

questions.stem: Which place in India gets more rain in a year than almost any other place in the world?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram, in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya near Cherrapunji, is one of the wettest places on Earth. Jaisalmer is in the Thar Desert and Leh is in the cold desert of Ladakh, where very little rain falls.

questions.stem: Which organ pumps blood to all parts of the body?
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscle that keeps pumping blood through the blood vessels. The lungs take in air for breathing.

questions.stem: What is the capital of Assam?
questions.explanation: Dispur is the capital of Assam. Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, Imphal of Manipur and Agartala of Tripura.

questions.stem: Bleeding gums can be a sign of too little of which vitamin, found in amla and oranges?
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, with bleeding gums. Amla, oranges and lemons are rich in it. Too little vitamin A causes night blindness.

questions.stem: Which harvest festival of Kerala is known for flower carpets, boat races and a grand feast?
questions.explanation: Onam is Kerala's harvest festival. Bihu is celebrated in Assam, Pongal in Tamil Nadu and Baisakhi in Punjab.

questions.stem: Why is milk boiled before we drink it?
questions.explanation: Boiling kills most germs in milk, so it is safe to drink and keeps longer. Boiling does not add vitamins or sugar.

questions.stem: Which crop is sown when the monsoon begins and grows in fields that stand under water?
questions.explanation: Rice needs a lot of water and is sown with the monsoon rains. Wheat, mustard and gram are sown in winter and need much less water.

questions.stem: Which habit helps to save water at home?
options: Leaving a leaking tap to drip
questions.explanation: Turning off the tap while you brush saves many litres every day. The other habits waste water.

questions.stem: Which shelter is built from blocks of hard snow in very cold, icy lands?
questions.explanation: An igloo is made of blocks of packed snow, which keeps the cold wind out. Stilt houses are raised on poles in places that flood.

questions.stem: Bats fly at night without bumping into things. Which sense helps them most?
questions.explanation: Bats make high sounds and listen for the echoes that bounce back from objects, so hearing guides them in the dark.

questions.stem: Which animal is called the ship of the desert?
questions.explanation: The camel can walk for days across hot sand with little water, carrying people and loads, so it is called the ship of the desert. The yak lives in cold mountains.

questions.stem: In which part of the body is most of our food digested and taken into the blood?
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth and stomach, but most of it finishes in the small intestine, where food passes into the blood. The large intestine mainly takes back water.

questions.stem: What do we call a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movements deep inside the Earth?
questions.explanation: An earthquake is the shaking of the ground. A cyclone is a storm with strong winds, a flood is too much water and a drought is too little rain.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what does the word 'chipko' mean?
questions.explanation: The passage says the word 'chipko' means 'to hug' or 'to stick to', which is what the women did to the trees.

questions.stem: Who led the women of Reni village?
questions.explanation: The passage says the group of women was led by Gaura Devi.

questions.stem: Why did the village women need the forests?
options: For timber to sell in cities
questions.explanation: The women collected firewood, fodder for their animals and fruits. Timber was what the workers were cutting the trees for.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what happens when trees on steep slopes are cut down?
questions.explanation: Tree roots hold the soil on slopes, so cutting the trees means more landslides and floods.

questions.stem: In which present-day state did the Chipko Movement begin?
questions.explanation: The passage places it in the Garhwal Himalaya, in today's Uttarakhand.

questions.stem: What is the place value of 7 in 4,73,215?
questions.explanation: 4,73,215 is four lakh seventy-three thousand two hundred fifteen. The 7 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 7 x 10,000 = 70,000.

questions.stem: How many grams are there in 3 kg 250 g?
How is 3,08,050 written in words?
questions.explanation: 3,08,050 is 3 lakh, 08 thousand and 050. Eighty thousand would be written 3,80,050.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 13 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 x (length + width) = 2 x (13 + 5) = 2 x 18 = 36 cm. 65 is the area in square centimetres.

questions.stem: What is 4,682 rounded to the nearest hundred?
questions.explanation: The tens digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so 4,682 rounds up to 4,700. 4,680 is the nearest ten, not hundred.

questions.stem: What is the area of a square with sides of 9 m?
questions.explanation: Area of a square = side x side = 9 x 9 = 81 square metres. 36 m is its perimeter.

questions.stem: What is the largest 4-digit number that can be made with the digits 5, 0, 3 and 8, using each digit once?
questions.explanation: Put the biggest digit in the thousands place and the rest in order from biggest to smallest: 8, 5, 3, 0. That gives 8,530.

questions.stem: A film starts at 2:45 pm and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. When does it end?
questions.explanation: 2:45 + 1 hour = 3:45. Then 15 minutes takes it to 4:00, and the other 35 minutes to 4:35 pm.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 6 and 9?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18. Multiples of 9: 9, 18. The first common multiple is 18. 54 is 6 x 9, common but not the lowest, and 3 is the HCF.

questions.stem: What kind of angle measures 150 degrees?
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. An acute angle is less than 90 degrees.

questions.stem: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 29 can be divided only by 1 and 29. 21 = 3 x 7, 27 = 3 x 9 and 33 = 3 x 11.

questions.stem: How many minutes are there in two and a half hours?
questions.explanation: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 hours = 120 minutes, and half an hour is 30 more: 150 minutes.

questions.stem: What is 2/9 + 5/9?
questions.explanation: For fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator: 2 + 5 = 7, so 7/9. Do not add the denominators.

questions.stem: A bottle holds 750 mL of water. How much do 4 such bottles hold?
questions.explanation: 4 x 750 mL = 3,000 mL. Since 1 litre = 1,000 mL, that is 3 litres.

questions.stem: What is the value of 48 ÷ 6 + 4 x 3?
questions.explanation: Divide and multiply before adding: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 4 x 3 = 12, so 8 + 12 = 20. Working left to right without this rule gives 36.

questions.stem:
The table shows how many books Ravi read on four days.

| Day | Books |
|---|---|
| Monday | 4 |
| Tuesday | 6 |
| Wednesday | 3 |
| Thursday | 7 |

How many books did he read in all?
questions.explanation: Add the column: 4 + 6 + 3 + 7 = 20.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 of 36?
questions.explanation: One quarter of 36 is 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so three quarters is 9 x 3 = 27.

questions.stem: On a map, the school is to the east of the park. In which direction is the park from the school?
questions.explanation: If the school is east of the park, you walk west to go from the school back to the park. Opposite directions swap.

questions.stem: A school has 1,248 students. 396 of them are girls. How many are boys?
A rectangle 10 cm long and 6 cm wide is cut along a diagonal into two equal triangles. What is the area of one triangle?
questions.explanation: The rectangle's area is 10 x 6 = 60 sq cm. The diagonal cuts it into two equal halves, so each triangle is 30 sq cm.

questions.stem: Why did Meena want a library?
options: She wanted to sell old books
Her teacher gave her the task
She had read all her school's books
questions.explanation: The passage says her school had only a few books and she had read all of them twice.

questions.stem: Where did Meena and her grandfather pin the notice?
options: On a pole by the river
questions.explanation: They pinned it to the big neem tree near the well.

questions.stem: 'Meena did not give up.' This means that she:
questions.explanation: Not giving up means continuing to try. She went from house to house until the shelf was full.

questions.stem: Which word is the opposite of 'proud'?
questions.explanation: To feel proud is to feel good about something you have done; to feel ashamed is to feel bad about it. Pleased and happy are close to proud.

questions.stem: Which is the best title for the passage?
options: Salim and the Big River Fish
questions.explanation: The whole story is about how Meena started a library for her village. The neem tree and the river are only small details.

questions.stem: According to the passage, an elephant's trunk is:
options: a part of its lower jaw
questions.explanation: The passage says the trunk is the elephant's nose and upper lip joined together. The long front teeth are tusks.

questions.stem: Who leads an elephant herd?
questions.explanation: Herds are led by the oldest female, who remembers the paths to water and food.

questions.stem: Why are elephants in danger, according to the passage?
questions.explanation: Elephants need large forests, so they are in danger when forests are cut down.

questions.stem: In the passage, the word 'honoured' means:
questions.explanation: To be honoured is to be given respect. The elephant is respected as India's national heritage animal.

questions.stem: Which use of the trunk is NOT mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage lists drinking, smelling, greeting, picking up a peanut and pulling down branches. Digging is not mentioned.

questions.stem: Where did Arjun and Neha fly their kite?
questions.explanation: Arjun climbed to the roof with Neha and ran across the roof to let the kite go.

questions.stem: What colour was their kite?
questions.explanation: The passage says their kite was red and yellow, with a long paper tail.

questions.stem: 'Arjun's face fell.' This means that Arjun:
questions.explanation: When someone's face falls, they suddenly look disappointed. Arjun was sad to lose the kite.

questions.stem: Why did the kite drift away?
questions.explanation: Another kite crossed theirs and the string snapped, so the kite drifted away.

questions.stem: What did the children do at the end of the story?
options: Went to find the old kite
Went to make a new kite
questions.explanation: The last sentence says they ran downstairs to make a new one.

questions.stem: Why do people call the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway the toy train?
options: It is painted like a toy
questions.explanation: Its engines and coaches are small and the track is narrow, so it looks like a toy.

questions.stem: How wide is the track of the toy train?
questions.explanation: The passage says the track is only about two feet wide.

questions.stem: How does the track climb the steep hills?
questions.explanation: The track goes round in loops and zigzags back and forth to climb the hills.

questions.stem: In which state does the toy train run?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says the railway runs in the hills of West Bengal.

questions.stem: In the passage, the word 'steep' means:
questions.explanation: A steep hill rises sharply, which is why the track needs loops and zigzags to climb it.

questions.stem: Which letter comes next? C, F, I, L, ...
questions.explanation: Each step moves three letters forward: C, F, I, L, then M, N, O. So the next letter is O.

questions.stem: A mirror is held beside each digit, to its right. Which digit looks exactly the same in the mirror?
questions.explanation: 8 has the same left half and right half, so its mirror image does not change. 2, 4 and 7 all look reversed.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 2, 5, 8, 11, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is 3 more than the one before it: 11 + 3 = 14.

questions.stem: A clock shows 4:30. What time does the clock seem to show when you look at it in a mirror?
questions.explanation: For a mirror clock, take the time away from 12:00. 12:00 - 4:30 = 7:30. Check: 4:30 + 7:30 = 12:00.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 100, 90, 81, 73, ...
questions.explanation: The amount taken away gets smaller by 1 each time: 10, 9, 8, then 7. So 73 - 7 = 66.

questions.stem: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, then folded in half again. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when it is opened?
questions.explanation: Two folds make four layers of paper, so one punch makes four holes.

questions.stem: Which pair comes next? AB, DE, GH, ...
questions.explanation: Each pair is two letters next to each other, and one letter is skipped between pairs (C, F, I). After GH, skip I to get JK.

questions.stem: In a triangle, one straight line is drawn from the top corner down to the middle of the base. How many triangles can be counted?
questions.explanation: The line makes 2 small triangles, and the whole big triangle is still there, so there are 3.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 2, 6, 18, 54, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is 3 times the one before it: 54 x 3 = 162. Doubling 54 would give 108, but 6 is 3 times 2, not 2 times.

questions.stem: Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror held to its right?
questions.explanation: A mirror reverses the order of the letters and flips each one. TOOT reads the same backwards and T and O look the same flipped. The N, B, K and D look reversed.

questions.stem: If 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C and so on, which word does 2-1-4 stand for?
questions.explanation: 2 is B, 1 is A and 4 is D, so 2-1-4 spells BAD.

questions.stem: Two squares of the same size are placed side by side so that one whole side of each touches. What shape do they make together?
questions.explanation: The new shape is twice as long as it is wide, with four right angles: a rectangle. Four equal squares would be needed to make a bigger square.

questions.stem: BAT is to TAB as POT is to:
questions.explanation: TAB is BAT written backwards. POT written backwards is TOP.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with all three sides equal have?
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle can be folded in half along a line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side, so it has 3 lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: Which letter group is the odd one out? ABC, DEF, GHJ, KLM
questions.explanation: In the other groups the three letters come one after another in the alphabet. GHJ skips I, so it does not follow the rule.

questions.stem: A dot moves around the corners of a square: top left, top right, bottom right, ... Where will it be next?
questions.explanation: The dot moves clockwise one corner at a time. After bottom right, the next corner clockwise is bottom left.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ...
questions.explanation: The amount added grows by 1 each time: +1, +2, +3, +4, then +5. So 11 + 5 = 16.

questions.stem: A long strip is divided into 3 equal boxes in a row. Counting the single boxes too, how many rectangles of any size can be seen?
questions.explanation: There are 3 single boxes, 2 rectangles made of two boxes side by side, and 1 made of all three: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

questions.stem: Which comes next? Z1, Y2, X3, ...
questions.explanation: The letters go backwards one at a time (Z, Y, X, W) and the numbers go up by one (1, 2, 3, 4).

questions.stem: Six equal squares joined edge to edge are folded up into a closed box. What solid shape is the box?
questions.explanation: A cube has six faces that are all equal squares, so six squares fold into a cube.

questions.stem: Which bird is the national bird of India?
questions.explanation: The peacock (Indian peafowl) is India's national bird, known for its colourful tail feathers.

questions.stem: Which nutrient helps the body grow and repair itself, and is found in pulses, eggs and milk?
questions.explanation: Proteins are body-building foods. Fats and starch mainly give energy, and fibre helps food move through the gut.

questions.stem: On the banks of which river does the city of Varanasi stand?
questions.explanation: Varanasi stands on the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh, with its famous ghats (steps) along the river. Delhi and Agra stand on the Yamuna.

questions.stem: Which organs do we use to breathe?
questions.explanation: The lungs take in air when we breathe in and let it out when we breathe out. The kidneys clean the blood.

questions.stem: What is the capital of Sikkim?
questions.explanation: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim. Kohima is the capital of Nagaland and Itanagar of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.stem: Milk and curd are rich in calcium. Calcium helps to keep which parts of our body strong?
questions.explanation: Calcium builds strong bones and teeth, which is why growing children are told to drink milk.

questions.stem: Which winter festival of Punjab is celebrated in January with a bonfire that families gather around?
questions.explanation: Lohri is celebrated in Punjab in January, around a bonfire with songs, peanuts and popcorn. Onam is from Kerala, Pongal from Tamil Nadu and Bihu from Assam.

questions.stem: Why do we keep cooked food in a refrigerator?
questions.explanation: Germs that spoil food grow very slowly in the cold, so food stays fresh longer. Cold does not add anything to food.

questions.stem: Jute is called the golden fibre. From which part of the jute plant does the fibre come?
questions.explanation: Jute fibre comes from the stem of the plant. Cotton is the fibre that grows around seeds, which is why seed is a tempting answer.

questions.stem: Which of these makes the air dirty?
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish gives off smoke and harmful gases that pollute the air. Trees help clean the air.

questions.stem: Houseboats on Dal Lake are a well-known kind of home in which city?
questions.explanation: Dal Lake is in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, and its houseboats are famous. Udaipur also has lakes, but not the houseboats of Dal Lake.

questions.stem: Which is the largest sense organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin covers the whole body and senses touch, heat, cold and pain, so it is the largest sense organ.

questions.stem: Water vapour high in the air cools and turns into tiny drops that form clouds. What is this step of the water cycle called?
questions.explanation: Condensation is vapour turning back into liquid drops. Evaporation is the opposite, liquid becoming vapour, and precipitation is the rain that falls.

questions.stem: Which illness can spread when mosquitoes breed in water collected in old tyres and coolers?
questions.explanation: Dengue is spread by mosquitoes that lay eggs in clean standing water, such as in coolers and tyres. Typhoid and cholera spread through dirty food and water.

questions.stem: The Rann of Kutch, a huge flat land of white salt, is in which state?
questions.explanation: The Rann of Kutch is in the Kutch district of Gujarat. In the dry months the ground dries into a wide white crust of salt.

questions.stem: What is a kund?
questions.explanation: The passage describes a kund as an underground tank shaped like a round bowl with a dome on top. A well with stairs is a baoli.

questions.stem: Why is the ground around a kund made to slope towards it?
options: So people can sit around it
So camels can drink from it
questions.explanation: The slope makes rainwater run into the tank, so as much rain as possible is collected.

questions.stem: What does the dome on top of a kund do?
questions.explanation: The dome keeps out dust and stops the water from drying up in the hot sun.

questions.stem: In which desert do these families live?
questions.explanation: The passage says the Thar Desert of western Rajasthan.

questions.stem: Where do the camels and goats get their water?
questions.explanation: The kund water is used for drinking by people; the passage says animals are given water from the village ponds.

questions.stem: What is the face value of 6 in 2,46,913?
questions.explanation: The face value of a digit is the digit itself, wherever it stands, so it is 6. Its place value would be 6,000.

questions.stem: How many centimetres are there in 4 m 5 cm?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm, so 4 m = 400 cm. 400 + 5 = 405 cm. 450 cm would be 4 m 50 cm.

questions.stem: How is 'five lakh four thousand nine' written in figures?
questions.explanation: Five lakh is 5,00,000, four thousand is 4,000 and nine is 9. Together: 5,04,009.

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of a square with sides of 15 cm?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 x 15 = 60 cm. 225 is its area in square centimetres.

questions.stem: What is 8,451 rounded to the nearest thousand?
questions.explanation: Look at the hundreds digit, 4. It is less than 5, so 8,451 rounds down to 8,000.

questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 8 m long and 6 m wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 8 x 6 = 48 square metres. 28 m is its perimeter.

questions.stem: Which shows 4,096, 4,690, 4,069 and 4,609 in ascending order (smallest first)?
questions.explanation: All start with 4, so compare the hundreds: 0 comes before 6. Then compare the tens: 4,069 before 4,096 and 4,609 before 4,690.

questions.stem: A train leaves at 22:40 and arrives 3 hours 35 minutes later. What time does it arrive, in 24-hour time?
questions.explanation: 22:40 + 3 hours = 25:40, which is 01:40 the next day. Adding 35 more minutes gives 02:15.

questions.stem: What is the HCF of 18 and 24?
questions.explanation: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The highest common factor is 6. 72 is the LCM.

questions.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at exactly 8 o'clock?
questions.explanation: The 12 numbers share a full turn of 360 degrees, so each gap is 360 / 12 = 30 degrees. At 8 o'clock the hands point to 12 and 8, four gaps apart going the short way round: 4 x 30 = 120 degrees. 240 degrees is the larger angle the long way round.

questions.stem: Which number is a factor of both 20 and 35?
questions.explanation: 20 = 4 x 5 and 35 = 7 x 5, so 5 divides both. 7 does not divide 20, and 4 and 10 do not divide 35.

questions.stem: How many minutes are there in 3 hours 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: 3 hours = 3 x 60 = 180 minutes. 180 + 20 = 200 minutes.

questions.stem: What is 7/12 - 3/12 in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: 7/12 - 3/12 = 4/12. Divide the top and bottom by 4: 4/12 = 1/3.

questions.stem: A pen costs ₹35 and a notebook costs ₹48. Meena pays for both with a ₹100 note. How much change does she get?
questions.explanation: The total cost is 35 + 48 = ₹83. Change = 100 - 83 = ₹17.

questions.stem: What is the value of 60 - 4 x (3 + 5)?
questions.explanation: Brackets first: 3 + 5 = 8. Then multiply: 4 x 8 = 32. Then subtract: 60 - 32 = 28.

questions.stem: In a pictograph, each ball picture stands for 4 balls. The row for Class 5A has 9 ball pictures. How many balls does Class 5A have?
questions.explanation: Each picture means 4 balls, so 9 pictures mean 9 x 4 = 36 balls. 13 comes from adding instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: What is 2/5 x 3/4?
questions.explanation: Multiply the tops and the bottoms: (2 x 3)/(5 x 4) = 6/20, which simplifies to 3/10.

questions.stem: A bar graph shows the favourite fruit of a class: mango 12 children, banana 8, apple 5 and guava 9. How many more children chose mango than guava?
questions.explanation: Mango 12 - guava 9 = 3 more children. 21 is what you get by adding them.

questions.stem: Rina has 3 boxes with 125 pencils in each. She gives away 87 pencils. How many pencils are left?
questions.explanation: 3 x 125 = 375 pencils. 375 - 87 = 288. Adding 87 instead of taking it away gives 462.

questions.stem: If 3 March is a Monday, what day of the week is 17 March?
questions.explanation: 17 - 3 = 14 days, which is exactly 2 weeks. The day of the week repeats every 7 days, so 17 March is also a Monday.

questions.stem: Where did Grandmother sit at her wheel?
questions.explanation: Every morning she sat at her wheel in the courtyard.

questions.stem: What happened to Raju's second pot?
questions.explanation: The second pot cracked as it dried in the sun. It was the first pot that leaned and collapsed.

questions.stem: Grandmother says, 'Clay teaches patience.' What does she want Raju to do?
options: Work as fast as he can
questions.explanation: She tells him her own first pots failed too. Patience means keeping on calmly until you succeed.

questions.stem: How many lamps did Raju make before Diwali?
questions.explanation: The passage says he made twelve small lamps that stood straight.

questions.stem: In the passage, the word 'glowed' means:
questions.explanation: The lamps were lit for Diwali, so they glowed, or shone with light.

questions.stem: How many queens does a honeybee colony have?
questions.explanation: The passage says a colony can have thousands of bees, but only one queen.

questions.stem: What do the young worker bees do?
questions.explanation: Young workers clean the cells and feed the baby bees. Older workers collect nectar, and the queen lays the eggs.

questions.stem: Why does a worker bee dance when she returns to the hive?
questions.explanation: Her dance tells the other bees the direction of the flowers and how far away they are.

questions.stem: Where do bees store their honey?
questions.explanation: Bees turn nectar into honey and store it in wax cells.

questions.stem: Why are bees important to farmers who grow fruit?
questions.explanation: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps plants make fruits and seeds.

questions.stem: Where did Fatima find the puppy?
questions.explanation: She heard a soft whimper under a parked cart.

questions.stem: Why did Fatima's mother frown at first?
questions.explanation: She was worried about the muddy paws, but then she brought a towel and warm milk.

questions.stem: In the passage, the word 'shivering' means:
questions.explanation: The puppy had been out in the rain, so it was wet and shaking with cold.

questions.stem: How did Kabir most likely find out where his puppy was?
questions.explanation: Fatima stuck a notice at the corner shop, and that same evening Kabir came running.

questions.stem: Which word best describes Fatima?
questions.explanation: She rescued a wet puppy, cared for it and found its owner, which shows she is kind.

questions.stem: According to the passage, when does the land become very hot?
questions.explanation: The passage says that in early summer the land becomes very hot, before the moist sea winds bring rain.

questions.stem: Why do farmers wait eagerly for the monsoon?
questions.explanation: Many crops, such as rice, depend on the monsoon rain.

questions.stem: According to the passage, too much rain can:
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says too much rain can flood towns and fields.

questions.stem: In the passage, the word 'moisture' means:
questions.explanation: Moisture is water in the air. The moist sea winds bring rain when they reach the land.

questions.stem: Which is the best title for the passage?
questions.explanation: The whole passage explains the monsoon: how it comes, why it matters and the trouble it can bring.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ...
questions.explanation: The amount added grows by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6. So 15 + 6 = 21.

questions.stem: A clock shows 2:00. What time does the clock seem to show when you look at it in a mirror?
questions.explanation: Take the time away from 12:00: 12:00 - 2:00 = 10:00. The hand pointing at 2 seems to point at 10.

questions.stem: Which letter comes next? D, H, L, P, ...
questions.explanation: Each step moves four letters forward: P, then Q, R, S, T. So the next letter is T.

questions.stem: Which of these capital letters looks the same when it is seen in a mirror placed to its right?
questions.explanation: U has the same left half and right half. L, P and G all face one way, so they look reversed in a side mirror.

questions.stem: If SUN is written as TVO, how is MAP written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter of SUN moves forward one place: S to T, U to V, N to O. So M becomes N, A becomes B and P becomes Q.

questions.stem: A sheet of paper is folded in half three times, each fold on top of the last. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when it is opened?
questions.explanation: Each fold doubles the layers: 2, then 4, then 8. One punch through 8 layers makes 8 holes.

questions.stem: Which number comes next? 64, 32, 16, 8, ...
questions.explanation: Each number is half of the one before it: half of 8 is 4.

questions.stem: A rectangle is cut along both of its diagonals. How many triangle pieces do you get?
questions.explanation: The two diagonals cross in the middle and cut the rectangle into 4 triangle pieces.

questions.stem: Which number is the odd one out? 11, 13, 17, 21, 23
questions.explanation: 11, 13, 17 and 23 are prime numbers, divisible only by 1 and themselves. 21 is 3 x 7, so it is not prime.

questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon (six equal sides) have?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon folds in half along the 3 lines joining opposite corners and the 3 lines joining the middles of opposite sides: 6 in all.

questions.stem: Which flower is the national flower of India?
questions.explanation: The lotus is India's national flower. It grows in ponds, with its leaves and flowers floating on the water.

questions.stem: Too little iron in our food can cause which problem?
questions.explanation: Iron helps make blood, so too little causes anaemia, which makes a person tired and pale. Green leafy vegetables and jaggery give iron.

questions.stem: What is the capital of Odisha?
questions.explanation: Bhubaneswar is the capital of Odisha. Cuttack and Puri are other cities of Odisha, and Ranchi is the capital of Jharkhand.

questions.stem: Which gas do our lungs take from the air for the body to use?
questions.explanation: We breathe in oxygen, which the body needs. We breathe out carbon dioxide. Most of the air is nitrogen, but the body does not use it.

questions.stem: Which mountain range stretches along the northern border of India?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas run along India's northern border. The Aravallis are in Rajasthan and the Western Ghats run along the west coast.

questions.stem: Farmers cut wide steps into hill slopes to grow crops. How do these steps help?
options: They keep birds off the crops
They warm the soil at night
questions.explanation: On a steep slope, rainwater rushes down and carries soil away. Flat steps slow the water, so the soil stays in place.

questions.stem: Which forest in the Ganga delta of West Bengal is famous for mangrove trees and the Bengal tiger?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is a mangrove forest where rivers meet the sea. Gir in Gujarat is known for lions and Kaziranga in Assam for one-horned rhinos.

questions.stem: Which habit keeps our teeth healthy?
questions.explanation: Brushing in the morning and before bed removes food and germs that cause tooth decay.

questions.stem: Silk thread comes from the cocoon of which creature?
questions.explanation: The silkworm spins a cocoon of fine silk thread, which is unwound to make silk cloth. Wool comes from sheep, and bees make honey and wax.

questions.stem: Which of these can be turned into compost in a garden pit?
questions.explanation: Vegetable peels rot and become compost that feeds plants. Plastic, glass and metal do not rot.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why do seeds need to travel away from the parent plant?
options: To find other seeds to join
To get space, light and water
questions.explanation: The passage says travelling helps the young plants get enough space, light and water.

questions.stem: How does a coconut travel to a faraway beach?
questions.explanation: Its hard shell and thick fibre let the coconut float on the sea.

questions.stem: Which seeds in the passage are carried away by the wind?
questions.explanation: Madar seeds have fine hairs and float away on the wind.

questions.stem: How do seeds with tiny hooks travel?
questions.explanation: The hooks catch on the fur of animals or on our clothes, and the seeds drop off somewhere else.

questions.stem: What happens to the pods of balsam when they dry?
questions.explanation: Dry balsam pods burst open with a snap and throw their seeds in all directions.

questions.stem: Which is the greatest number?
questions.explanation: All start with 9 thousand. Compare the hundreds: 9,990 and 9,909 both have 9, then the tens: 9 is more than 0, so 9,990 is greatest.

questions.stem: How many metres are there in 2 km 60 m?
What is the LCM of 4 and 10?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 10 are 10, 20, 30... The first one that 4 also divides is 20. 2 is the HCF, not the LCM.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: The perimeter is the distance all the way round: 7 + 8 + 9 = 24 cm.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorisation of 60?
questions.explanation: 60 = 2 x 30 = 2 x 2 x 15 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 5, and each of these is prime. 1 and 4 are not prime, and the other two multiply to 90 and 120.

questions.stem: What kind of angle is smaller than a right angle?
questions.explanation: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. An obtuse angle is between 90 and 180 degrees, and a straight angle is exactly 180 degrees.

questions.stem: What is the value of 100 - 25 x 2?
questions.explanation: Multiply first: 25 x 2 = 50, then 100 - 50 = 50. Subtracting first gives (100 - 25) x 2 = 150.

questions.stem: How many days are there in February 2028?
questions.explanation: 2028 can be divided exactly by 4, so it is a leap year and February has 29 days.

questions.stem: What is 1/8 + 5/8 in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: 1/8 + 5/8 = 6/8, and dividing the top and bottom by 2 gives 3/4.

questions.stem:
The table shows trees planted by three classes.

| Class | Trees |
|---|---|
| Class 3 | 15 |
| Class 4 | 20 |
| Class 5 | 25 |

How many trees were planted in all?
How long had Ravi practised for the race?
questions.explanation: He had practised every morning for a month.

questions.stem: Why did Ravi stop running?
questions.explanation: Imran had tripped and was holding his knee. It was Imran, not Ravi, who was hurt.

questions.stem: In what place did Ravi and Imran finish the race?
questions.explanation: The passage says both boys came last.

questions.stem: What did the head teacher give Ravi?
questions.explanation: At the prize ceremony he was given a special badge for kindness.

questions.stem: What lesson does the story teach?
questions.explanation: The head teacher says winning is good but helping a friend is better.

questions.stem: Where are lighthouses built?
questions.explanation: The passage says a lighthouse is built on a rocky coast or on a small island.

questions.stem: How can sailors tell one lighthouse from another?
options: By the sound of its bell
questions.explanation: Each lighthouse flashes in its own pattern, so sailors count the flashes.

questions.stem: Why are many lighthouses painted in bright stripes?
options: To be seen in the day
questions.explanation: The stripes make lighthouses easy to see in the day, when the lamp is not needed.

questions.stem: In the passage, 'work automatically' means the lighthouses work:
questions.explanation: Automatic means working without a person, unlike the old keepers who kept the lamp burning.

questions.stem: Who kept the lamp burning in the past?
questions.explanation: In the past, a keeper lived in the tower and kept the lamp burning all night.
